bug_semantics: ZeroBrew's Ruby formula compatibility shim downloaded secondary formula resources and URL-based patches with curl and then extracted or applied them during `zb install --build-from-source` without ever comparing the bytes to the sha256 values the formula DSL had already parsed. In zb_io/src/build/shim.rb, StagedResource.stage stored @sha256 but after Kernel.system("curl", "-sSL", "-o", archive, @url) immediately called extract_resource; the URL-patch loop stored p[:sha256] but after curl wrote tmp.path immediately ran patch -i. A network attacker who can substitute those URLs (MITM or compromised host) can inject attacker-controlled archives or diffs that execute as build steps with no integrity warning. Primary formula tarballs in zb_io/src/build/source.rs already verified SHA-256; only the shim resource/patch paths omitted the check. CWE-494.
flaw_origin: The download-without-verify mechanism was first written in 5e9da9406db4630bf1cf0dc62581b9fff15bc9b4 (feat(zb_io): expand ruby shim DSL coverage for production readiness), which replaced no-op Formula.resource/patch stubs with PatchDSL/ResourceDSL parsers that captured sha256 plus StagedResource curl+extract and a curl+patch URL loop that never read those checksums. Immediate parent 7fd73e98b7ce12a0e13140d8c802c32d3663f03b still had `def resource(_name, &block) = nil` / `def patch(opts = {}, &block) = nil` and no curl. Neighboring same-batch commit 71dfd5b already normalized checksums for the primary tarball fetch, so the omission is specific to this shim expansion, not a later regression.
